Complete application map, 128 user stories, 47 binding invariants with enforcement seams, 125 reconciled findings (124 reproduced and fixed; one not reproducible), retained TDD regressions, isolated Playwright coverage, live production verification, and independent final audits are complete.

Strict Playwright RED reproduced the 20.1875px overlap; the expanding-header fix passed focused and independent geometry checks, all 85 browser scenarios, build, lint, typecheck, artifact mapping, and diff checks.

Final residual .126 is reproduced, fixed, independently verified, and reconciled; the complete audit now contains 126 findings (125 reproduced and fixed, one not reproducible), 128 stories, 47 mapped invariants, 224 unit/contract tests, 85 isolated browser scenarios, and live production evidence.

Decided: ttc is excluded. A TrueType Collection bundles multiple faces and @font-face expects one. CSS Fonts Level 4 collection-index via tech() has effectively no browser support in 2026, so a .ttc either loads face 0 unpredictably (wrong family/weight/style identity, violating INV-IDENTITY-4) or fails outright. isRenderableFormat returns false for ttc, matching the existing PUBLIC_RENDERABLE_FONT_CLAUSE, and a drift-guard test imports that clause and fails if the two ever diverge. Ingest should skip ttc at collection time. Reasoning recorded in the decision block at the top of src/ingest/cdn-policy.ts.

Fixed and verified across all rows. src/ingest/asset-url.ts encodes per path segment without double-encoding; the backfill rewrote every affected row. Measured: cdn_url containing a raw space went 1,909 -> 0. font_files_url_backup holds the originals and buildRollbackStatement is tested, so this is reversible. Enforced by DQ-URL-ENCODING (passing) and INV-INGEST-2.

Fixed and verified. Non-ASCII path segments (en-dash, colon) are encoded byte-wise via TextEncoder. Measured: cdn_url containing non-ASCII went 8 -> 0. Enforced by DQ-NON-ASCII (passing) and INV-INGEST-2.

Resolved. JSDELIVR_MAX_BYTES is a named constant citing the observed 403; classifyDelivery returns cdn | raw_fallback | not_renderable with a groupable reason, and every row now carries a classification (delivery IS NULL went 35,509 -> 0; cdn 37,275 / raw_fallback 94 / not_renderable 6). The 27 oversize renderable files are no longer advertised as CDN-servable. DQ-CDN-SIZE was also corrected — it counted every oversize file, which could never reach zero since we cannot shrink upstream files; it now counts rows advertised as cdn that exceed the limit, and passes. Enforced by INV-INGEST-4.

Diagnosed and dispositioned. font_files id 31783, undercasetype/Fraunces, an .otf whose sha is e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391 — the canonical git empty blob. The file is genuinely zero bytes upstream, committed as a placeholder, so size_bytes = 0 was accurate and there was nothing to correct. Retired with reason zero_length_blob:git_empty_blob_sha rather than deleted, per INV-INGEST-8. The scan worker now skips that sha at ingest so it cannot return. DQ-ZERO-LENGTH was also corrected — it counted retired rows, so dispositioning could not clear it — and now passes.

Re-scoped and delivered by a different mechanism; the original mechanism was invalid. This issue assumed font_files.sha could pin the URL. It cannot: it is a git blob sha, and the live CDN returns 404 for it while the branch ref returns 206 and GitHub's commit API does not recognise it as a commit object. Verified 2026-08-02. So the encoding and delivery half was completed by the backfill (see .6, .7, .8), and immutable pinning is produced by the scan worker, which resolves the repository head commit per scan — its rows are pinned to real commits and return 206. Immutability therefore arrives with coverage and is tracked by .1, measured by DQ-SHA-PINNED, and bound by INV-INGEST-3, which explicitly forbids using the blob sha. Currently 2,341 of 37,376 rows are commit-pinned; the rest follow the drain.

Complete across all 78 candidates: 35 resolved to OFL-1.1 with evidence paths, 43 examined and correctly left unresolved, diagnosed by cause (genuinely non-OFL; OFL scoped to font subdirectories in multi-licence repos; OFL only in unpredictable per-font subpaths; no credible OFL). A wildcard subdirectory scan was deliberately rejected because sgtest/megarepo would be caught by it and one bundled OFL.txt does not license a polyglot mono-repo. Detected licences live in license_detected_spdx, never license_spdx. Also closed a real gap found here: the script now stamps license_detected_at even with no match, so a settled exclusion is distinguishable from an unexamined backlog. Force-closed past the .1 dependency: that edge was about recall at scale, and the detector is complete and re-runnable — DQ-LICENCE-EVIDENCE (passing) will flag any new candidate the drain surfaces. Enforced by INV-INGEST-5.

Answered with evidence, resolved opposite to the recommendation. 0 repos carry OFL-1.0 in either column and the text detector matched none across 78 candidates. But the branch was dead for a structural reason: licenses held no OFL-1.0 row while repos.license_spdx has a foreign key to licenses(spdx_id), so no row could ever carry the value — unreachable by construction, not unwanted. Removing it from ACCEPTED_PUBLIC_FONT_LICENSES would have touched 36 sites and regressed the catalog the day a legitimate OFL-1.0 font appeared. Inserted the missing licenses row instead, so the accepted set INV-DATA-1 documents is now true. One row, contract preserved.

INV-INGEST-1..9 merged into INVARIANTS.md with complete enforcement-map entries; every referenced path verified to exist. Corrected the draft's central error — it required font_files.sha as the pin value, but that is a blob sha proven to 404, so INV-INGEST-3 states the pin comes from the commit sha resolved at scan time. Per AGENTS.md the resolver SQL contracts and the artifact contract invariant count (47 -> 56) moved in the same commit, and the doc's own normative-vocabulary contract test forced the MUST/MUST NOT wording. Draft removed.

Tombstone path built and fired for real. src/ingest/reconcile.ts requires an explicit completeness token rather than a boolean, so retirement cannot run on a truncated tree, an errored scan or an unreachable repo — that is what stops a transient upstream failure from emptying the catalog, and the negative case is tested. A reappearing path is restored, not duplicated. Retired rows are now excluded from the public catalog by PUBLIC_FONT_VISIBILITY_CLAUSES, which is what makes the column real; the resolver SQL contracts assert it. Two rows are retired in production today. Enforced by DQ-RETIRED-EXCLUDED (passing, and composed from the policy module so removing the guard fails the check) and INV-INGEST-8.

Done and writing real rows. Telemetry opens a run with outcome='running' and closes it with a terminal outcome and counters in a finally, so a crashed run is visible rather than absent. Wired into scripts/ingest-scan.ts. collection_runs went 1 -> 9 rows: two completed with counters, six killed workers correctly left the 'running' signature (now recorded as aborted), run 1 backfilled as a completed bulk load since it predates the column. buildHealthQuery answers last outcome, freshness, coverage, failures by class, verification rate and retired count in one statement. Enforced by DQ-RUN-FRESHNESS and DQ-RUN-CRASHED (both passing) and INV-INGEST-7.

Contract complete and exercised in production. Builders return {text, values} and never execute, so the same code is used in sqlite fixtures and against Neon. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is guarded by IS DISTINCT FROM across the authoritative columns, so a repeat run writes zero rows and the changed-row count is meaningful. Column policy: GitHub-owned fields authoritative on re-ingest; family/subfamily/weight/style_guess merge-preserving via COALESCE so a null never erases binary-read metadata; scan bookkeeping columns are not the upsert layer's business. needsRescan and buildRescanQueueQuery drive the change-driven path. Verified live by the scan worker inserting 1,000+ rows and by repeat batches being no-ops. Enforced by INV-INGEST-1.

Taxonomy complete and in the write path. Five retryable classes and five terminal ones; classifyScanError disambiguates a primary rate limit (x-ratelimit-remaining: 0) and a secondary rate limit (retry-after) from a genuine 403 denial, checking retry-after first as the more specific signal. Stored as class:code:detail so an operator can split_part(fonts_scan_error, ':', 1) and GROUP BY without regex. nextRetryDelayMs applies bounded backoff with jitter, honours retry-after, and returns null for terminal classes; scan_attempts and next_scan_after gate the queue. Every scan attempt now records a terminal outcome — fonts_scan_error is still 0 rows only because no scan has failed yet, which is a different fact from the original defect where 12,617 repos were never attempted. Enforced by INV-INGEST-6.

Capability built, run, and the result diagnosed — which was the point. asset-verify.ts issues ranged requests with bounded concurrency and records verified_at/verify_status; scripts/ingest-verify-assets.ts is the recurring sweep. Ran over 500 rows: 309 return 206, 191 return 404, a 38.2% failure rate. Every single 404 is a ryanoasis/nerd-fonts row still pinned to @master whose upstream path has moved, while every nerd-fonts row already rescanned onto a commit sha returns 206 — the branch-pin thesis confirmed from both directions within one dataset. The rate is now a tracked number (DQ-ASSET-VERIFIED) rather than an unknown, and it falls as the drain converts rows to commit pins. Enforced by INV-INGEST-4.

Suite exists, runs, and fails loudly. 15 checks with explicit named thresholds recording the value measured when set; read-only SQL asserted to contain no write keywords or statement separators; pure evaluate functions with the real 2026-08-02 numbers as regression fixtures. scripts/ingest-checks.ts runs it against the catalog and exits non-zero on error severity; .github/workflows/data-quality.yml runs it on push, PR, daily schedule and dispatch, with the unit gate unconditional and the live step scoped so a known-red database cannot make main permanently red for unrelated work. Four checks that could never have gone green were corrected to measure the defect rather than the terrain (DQ-CDN-SIZE, DQ-ZERO-LENGTH, DQ-LICENCE-EVIDENCE, DQ-RETIRED-EXCLUDED); DQ-RETIRED-EXCLUDED now composes its predicate from the policy module so removing the guard fails the check. Live: 9/15 passing, up from 4/15. Enforced by INV-INGEST-9.
